label: At D2, update gate stays high for S2, dips for S1, deeper when S1 believed good and late.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * belief ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * ep_dec
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2)*(prev_action==1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * (action==2)
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 25 sits near 0.98 at D1/GO and drops at D2 (timing). Beyond timing, almost everything is the reached state shown at D2: reaching S2 keeps z high (~+0.13 to +0.14), reaching S1 lowers it, and the S1 dip deepens as the ideal observer grows more confident S1 is good (belief_lo) and later in the episode (ep_dec). All observed at D2, no future variables. Previous-trial pattern and D1/GO effects are tiny (<0.03). The free fit adds the choice x state interaction (a2 into S1, i.e. rare, dips less than a1 into S1; a2 into S2 is highest) and a small D1 dip after a1->S2 trials, raising dev R^2 from 0.90 to 0.92.

issues: The belief_lo term has the wrong shape. Linear belief fits much better: replacing (state==S1)*belief_lo with (state==S1)*belief raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.898 to 0.938. Two terms alone, S2 ;; S1*belief, reach 0.923, which beats the recorded three-term form.

The 'deeper late' claim is mostly an artifact of the belief_lo shape. With belief_lo, the S1*ep_dec weight is -0.020 and dropping the term costs a lot (0.898 -> 0.717). With linear belief, the ep_dec weight shrinks to -0.008 and dropping it costs only 0.938 -> 0.923. Late-episode deepening is a minor effect, not a main driver.

Systematic misses on the recorded short form: the worst-fit windows are all EARLY-episode (t2-t17) S1 visits. Actual z is about 0.60-0.68 but the prediction is about 0.79-0.84, because belief_lo is near 0 early and the form under-predicts the dip. D2 errors also run negative on average (-0.010), with D2 after a1 S1 r at -0.024 and after a1 S2 u at -0.022. With linear belief these errors shrink to at most about 0.02 and the phase means to about 0.001.

The free-fit 'choice x state' story mostly overlaps with belief. (state==S1)*(action==1) in place of belief gives 0.938 with ep_dec and 0.909 without, about the same as belief, because a1 is chosen when S1 is believed good. The label cannot cleanly separate 'common a1->S1' from 'S1 believed good'.

Directional claims do check out. S2 keeps z high (+0.14), the S1 dip deepens with belief that S1 is good (weight -0.156 on belief), all terms are observed-only, and D1/GO effects are small (under 0.025).
